Upgrading an existing project

Source: vignettes/upgrading-a-project.qmd

This vignette covers projects that were created or last repaired with an older boosterpak. upgrade_project() brings them up to the installed version. It repairs the managed .Rprofile startup lines and boosters/attach.R, installs missing workflow packages into the project library, and records the result in renv.lock. It does not change your pack declarations, your boosters.toml settings, or your helper functions. The only boosters.toml change is the boosters_version record.

Who needs it

A project needs an upgrade when it was last migrated with an older boosterpak. boosters.toml records that version in [project].boosters_version:

[project]
name = "my-project"
# boosters_version is the boosterpak version this project was last migrated
# with. init() and the upgrade path refresh it; sync() does not. It is not a
# lock. When it is older than the installed boosterpak, run
# boosterpak::upgrade_project() to bring the project up to date.
boosters_version = "0.9.2"

status() warns when the recorded version is older than the installed boosterpak. A missing record is reported as “no version recorded” without a warning, and upgrade_needed is still TRUE. You do not need to know which layout a project has. The dry run below shows what would change.

sync() does not update the recorded version. A project that only ran sync() after an upgrade of boosterpak still needs upgrade_project().

Before you start

  • Commit or stash your work, so that the upgrade shows up as its own diff.
  • Run the upgrade from the R version the project should pin. The lockfile records the R version that runs the upgrade.
  • Have a GitHub token ready if the install step may run. See “GitHub rate limits” below.

The recipe

The order matters. Run the dry run before the real upgrade, and review the diff before you commit.

flowchart TD
  A([Commit or stash your work]) --> B(["Install the new boosterpak into the project library"])
  B --> C(["Restart R in the project"])
  C --> D(["upgrade_project(dry_run = TRUE)"])
  D --> E["Read the preview: R version, CRAN URL, packages, files"]
  E --> F(["upgrade_project()"])
  F --> G(["git diff"])
  G --> H([Commit])
  G --> I(["Revert the files under Files touched"])

  classDef userAction fill:#e8f3ff,stroke:#1f6feb,color:#0b1f3a;
  classDef packageAction fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#6e7781,color:#24292f;
  class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I userAction;

1. Install the new boosterpak

Update the copy in the project library, so that renv.lock can record the new version:

renv::install("seanthimons/boosterpak")

Then restart R in the project, so the new version is the one that loads.

upgrade_project() installs workflow packages only when they are missing from the project library. It does not update a copy that is already there, so this step is the one that moves the project’s boosterpak forward.

2. Run a dry run 

boosterpak::upgrade_project(dry_run = TRUE)

A dry run changes no files, installs no packages, and restores the session options it touched. It prints the planned actions and the report. When verbose is left at its default, a dry run always prints.

3. Read the preview

The report ends with a Lockfile preview (renv.lock) section and a Files a real run would touch list. The preview has three parts:

  • R version, the version recorded in renv.lock and the version that is running the upgrade. A change here means the lockfile will pin a different R version. Start R at the version you want before continuing.
  • CRAN repository, the URL recorded in the lockfile and the URL in use now.
  • The workflow packages (renv, pak, boosterpak) and their dependencies whose locked version differs from the installed version, one per line in the form package: locked -> installed.

The preview is an estimate. renv writes the final records when the snapshot runs.

4. Run the upgrade 

boosterpak::upgrade_project()

In an interactive session the report prints by default. In a script, pass verbose = TRUE to see it.

To leave renv.lock alone, pass snapshot = FALSE. The upgrade still repairs the project files and installs missing workflow packages, but it does not write the lockfile. Run upgrade_project() again without that argument before you commit, or the lockfile keeps its old records.

5. Review and commit or revert 

git diff

Commit when the diff matches the preview. To undo the upgrade:

  1. Restore each tracked file listed under “Files touched” with git restore.
  2. For each new file the upgrade created, such as boosters/packs/core.toml, check the path first with git clean -n -- <path>, then remove it with git clean -f -- <path>. Use only the paths the report lists.
  3. Restart R.

Packages installed into renv/library/ are not tracked by git. Remove them with renv::remove() if you do not want them.

Files the upgrade touches

Each file is touched only when the condition in the middle column holds. .Rprofile, boosters/packs/core.toml, and the declared pack files are reported as skipped when they are already current. boosters/attach.R and renv.lock are rewritten or re-snapshotted on every run where they apply, so they are listed under “Files touched” even when nothing changed.

File When it is touched Why
.Rprofile The managed startup block or the repository lines differ from the current layout Replaces an older hook block, removes historical hook lines, and adds the Linux binary lines. Other lines are kept.
boosters/attach.R Every run where boosters.toml is valid Rewritten in the current guarded format. When [attach].enabled = false, a managed file is removed instead.
boosters/packs/core.toml Only when missing Materializes the built-in core pack manifest.
boosters/packs/ Only for declared packs whose files are not yet present Copies pack manifests and nested helper sidecars. Existing files are not overwritten.
renv.lock Unless snapshot = FALSE Records renv, pak, boosterpak, and their hard dependencies, along with the R version and the CRAN URL. Other packages keep their records.
renv/activate.R Only when the renv version changes during the snapshot renv rewrites its activation script when it records a new renv version.
boosters.toml Only when [project].boosters_version is missing or older than the installed boosterpak, and the run reports no warnings Sets boosters_version to the installed version. No other field changes. A dry run only lists the file.

boosters/fn_*.R helper files are not rewritten. Your local edits to them are kept.

What changes in renv.lock

  • R version. The R record is set to the R version that runs the upgrade.
  • CRAN repository. The lockfile records the generic Package Manager URL, such as https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest, even on glibc Linux, where the session uses a manylinux binary URL. The upgrade’s snapshot passes the generic URL to renv, so the __linux__/manylinux_2_28 segment does not reach renv.lock. A manual renv::snapshot() does not get that handling; renv strips the segment only while its own Package Manager handling is on. See “Linux binary packages” in vignette("getting-started", package = "boosterpak").
  • Package records. renv, pak, boosterpak, and their hard dependencies are recorded at their installed versions.
  • Repository and Platform fields. Packages installed from Package Manager binaries can carry Repository: RSPM and a Linux Platform tag. After its snapshot, upgrade_project() removes the Linux Platform tags and replaces any Repository URL with the matching repository name, or with the generic Package Manager URL. RSPM stays; it is a repository name, and restore falls back to the repository URLs in renv.lock. Those are the generic Package Manager URLs, which also serve Windows and macOS binaries. To check, run git diff -- renv.lock | grep -E '^\+.*("Platform"|__linux__)'; it should print nothing. Check each platform after its first restore.

The managed .Rprofile block over time

The startup lines have changed in each release. upgrade_project() replaces the older forms with the current one.

Layout What the .Rprofile contains
0.5.x One line that sources the boosters/fn_*.R files. No attachment.
0.6.1 to 0.7.0 One line that sources boosters/attach.R, then the fn_*.R files. No markers.
0.8.0 to 0.9.2 The same line wrapped in a managed block, # BEGIN boosterpak managed startup to # END boosterpak managed startup, inside try(). The repository and install-policy lines sit around the activation line. 0.9.2 also adds the early Linux binary line (manylinux).
Current source (next release) The block sources boosters/attach.R and each fn_*.R file in its own try(), so one failure does not stop the rest. The Linux binary lines are also repeated after the renv activation line.

The reason for the last change is that attach.R loads packages. In the 0.8.0 to 0.9.2 layout, a missing package made attach.R fail, and that stopped the helper files that came after it. In the current layout, attach.R attaches each package on its own, so a missing package is reported and the rest still attach.

The post-activation Linux lines matter because renv/activate.R calls renv::load(). That resets repos to the lockfile URLs and undoes the manylinux rewrite made before activation. The lines repeat the rewrite right after activation, and only while renv’s Package Manager handling is on. They keep the lockfile URL generic. See “Linux binary packages” in vignette("getting-started", package = "boosterpak").

A rerun is safe. On a second run the .Rprofile lines are not rewritten, because they already match, and the report lists .Rprofile and the pack files as skipped. boosters/attach.R is regenerated with the same content, and renv.lock is re-snapshotted. Both stay listed under “Files touched”, so check them with git diff. boosters.toml is listed only when its boosters_version changes. On a rerun that finds the version current, the report says so as a skipped step.

GitHub rate limits

The install step runs only when a workflow package is missing from the project library. boosterpak is installed from GitHub only when it is the missing package. Anonymous GitHub requests are limited, so that install can fail with a rate limit. When it does, upgrade_project() does not stop. It reports a WARNING: workflow package install skipped line, with a hint that names the token options appended to it. The run then writes no renv.lock and does not record boosters_version. Set a token and rerun. The first step of this recipe, renv::install("seanthimons/boosterpak"), also talks to GitHub, but renv reports its own errors, so no boosterpak hint is added there.

Set a token before you run either step. From a shell where the GitHub CLI is logged in:

GITHUB_PAT=$(gh auth token) Rscript -e 'boosterpak::upgrade_project(".")'

The substitution passes the token to that one command. The token is not written to a file, and boosterpak never prints its value. For the other ways to supply a token, and what to keep out of the project, see “GitHub rate limits” in vignette("restoring-a-project", package = "boosterpak").

Troubleshooting

The report prefixes each line with OK:, INFO:, or WARNING:. INFO lines are skips, which do not stop the run. WARNING lines are problems. A run with any warning does not record boosters_version. Most entries below quote a report line. The first entry is an error that stops the run.

boosters.toml does not exist. The directory is not a boosterpak project, or boosters.toml was deleted. upgrade_project() repairs existing projects only. Use init() for a new project, or restore the file from git.

workflow package repair skipped: no project renv found. The project has no project-local renv. The .Rprofile and attach.R repairs still run, but the workflow packages are not installed or snapshotted. Run boosterpak::init(renv = "yes") to create one, then upgrade again.

workflow package repair skipped: renv is unavailable. renv is not installed, so the workflow packages are not repaired or snapshotted. The report also carries a WARNING: workflow package repair incomplete line, so the run does not record boosters_version. Install renv into your user library and rerun.

WARNING: workflow package repair skipped: project renv could not be loaded. The upgrade could not activate the project’s renv. Fix the error it reports, then rerun. Nothing is written to renv.lock on this path.

boosters.toml is not valid for config-dependent repairs. The file parses, but a field the upgrade needs is the wrong type. The message names the field. Fix it and rerun. Pack materialization and attach.R are skipped until then, but the .Rprofile repair still runs.

WARNING: workflow package install skipped, with a GitHub hint. The install failed, most often with a GitHub rate limit. The .Rprofile and attach.R repairs are already done, but the run writes no renv.lock and does not record boosters_version. Set a token as shown above, then rerun.

WARNING: workflow package snapshot skipped. The packages are installed, but the dependency check or renv::snapshot() failed. The message carries renv’s error. Fix it and rerun.

boosters_version not recorded: the upgrade reported warnings. This is an INFO line. The version is recorded only after a run with no warnings, so fix the warnings above and rerun. A WARNING: boosters_version not recorded: <reason> line means the record itself could not be written. The message gives the reason.

lockfile preview unavailable. The dry run could not read renv.lock. The rest of the report is still valid. Check that the file parses, for example with jsonlite::validate().

repository configuration skipped: disabled by option or environment. Repository setup is off, because BOOSTERPAK_CONFIGURE_REPOSITORIES=false or the boosterpak.configure_repositories option is set. This is an INFO line. If install-policy setup is still on, the rerun removes the managed repository lines from .Rprofile, because boosterpak has no repository setup to write back. The install-policy lines are kept. If install-policy setup is off as well, BOOSTERPAK_CONFIGURE_INSTALL_POLICY=false or the boosterpak.configure_install_policy option is FALSE, no setup lines are written, and the existing repository and install-policy lines are not changed.

repository configuration already set or intentionally custom. This is information, not a problem. boosterpak leaves a custom CRAN repository alone.

attach file rewrite skipped. The message gives the reason. The other repairs still run.
